## Evidence matrix

| Source and stage | Attempt, feedback and update | Observed outcome and limit |
|---|---|---|
| **S0234, initial build** | A nonempty Blender program constructed separate scene elements, materials, camera and lights. Step 1 executed and its render was selected. | Execution returned `ok: true` and saved a render and blend file; this establishes technical execution, not visual fidelity or connected geometry. The log reported 16 samples although the program requested 48. [S0234, lines 3–6] |
| **S0234, revision** | The student received the reference and first render for comparison, then executed a complete revision changing the sink construction, tiles, camera, lighting and exposure. No verbal diagnosis is visible. | Step 2 also returned `ok: true`, saved outputs and was selected, again with 16 samples reported. Whether the revision improved the match or closed basin gaps is unknown. [S0234, lines 7–12] |
| **S0234, final response** | A fresh session received references to the original and both renders, made no tool calls and replied `DONE` after the execution budget was exhausted. | Protocol completion is not independent visual validation or a formal quality score. [S0234, lines 13–15] |
| **S0235, first execution** | A nonempty scene program was executed. A sink-rim fillet radius exceeded half the smallest dimension; the resulting error was sent to the student. | Execution failed before rendering, with a null image. This was a build failure, not an empty patch. [S0235, lines 3–6] |
| **S0235, second execution and final proposal** | The student reduced the fillet radius and made other scene changes. The second execution passed the first failure point but failed because the scene world was `None`. That error and the exhausted execution budget were sent to the student. A final program proposed creating a world and changing the cabinet construction. | The second image was also null. The final program was not executed, so its fix and scene quality remain unverified. [S0235, lines 8–11, 13] |

## Synthesis

Both trajectories address a single-image, separate-mesh indoor reconstruction with viewpoint, framing, placement and materials to match. The programs interpret the scene as a kitchen; the audit does not independently verify that interpretation against the reference image. Their sink, cabinet, tile, material and camera choices are therefore task-specific facts, not general prescriptions. [S0234, lines 1, 3–4, 7–10; S0235, lines 1, 3–4, 8–9]

The contrast is between **technically successful rendering with unknown reconstruction quality** in S0234 and **two failed builds followed by an unexecuted proposal** in S0235. S0235 provides a partial progression past one runtime error, not a successful render. S0234 provides an executed visual-iteration cycle, but the trace does not expose the student’s diagnosis or independently establish that the revision helped. Neither case supports an algorithmic superiority claim. No permission, branch or CLI stop is reported in these trajectories; the relevant interruption in S0235 was exhaustion of the execution budget, while S0234 ended after its budget was exhausted. [S0234, lines 5–15; S0235, lines 5–13]

For teacher involvement, the supplied student-trajectory audits report no teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, receipt or adoption. Thus teacher advice availability is not established, and there is no visible teacher-advice-to-update chain to assess. S0234’s image-comparison request and S0235’s delivered runtime errors were runner feedback, not teacher advice. The former was followed by an executed revision; the latter by an executed revision and then an unexecuted proposal. Selection of S0234’s renders is recorded, but neither final acceptance of visual quality nor an independent quality assessment is shown. [S0234, lines 6–12, 14–15; S0235, lines 5–13]

The transferable evidentiary constraint is to keep execution, feedback receipt, update execution and quality verification separate: saved renders do not prove fidelity or part contact, and advancing past an error does not prove a correct scene. S0234 is a counterexample to treating every attempt as a build failure; S0235 is a counterexample to treating a plausible final fix as an observed success. Whether S0234’s altered camera or assembled basin improved the match, and whether S0235’s final world initialization or cabinet change would work, are hypotheses only. Formal scores are unknown, and old model cost cannot be recovered from their absence.

## Coverage

This report covers the supplied audit reports for both files in **scene / scene_rsi_v2_1__smoke, batch 1 of 1**: S0234, chunks 1–2, and S0235, chunk 1. File counts include copies and should not be interpreted as counts of independent trials. The reports cover the source material supplied for this batch; the underlying image pixels are not visible in the audits, limiting independent assessment of appearance, geometry and reference matching.
